newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian stocks amble to firmer close.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian stocks amble to firmer close.

text.p: SPI Futures 2467 +7 US 30yr cl 6.82 steady
10yrbond futs 92.200 +0.015 Gold NY 351.75 Lon fix 350.25
*Stocks end firmer but well off early highs as initial interest abates, News tops turnover. Volume 414.52 million, value A$960.73 million, 1,104 stocks traded, 332 steady, 391 up, 381 down.
A mixed Australian share market ended in firmer territory on Tuesday but well off its early Dow-inspired highs as initial enthusiasm quickly abated.
By 4.25 p.m. (0525 GMT), the All Ordinaries index was 6.4 points higher at 2,468.3 after touching an intraday high of 2,476.3.
The March share index futures contract was seven points higher at 2,467, a 1.3 point discount to the underlying index.
Brokers said that while the market had made a strong start, there had been insufficient interest to keep the early upside momentum going.
"It started off full of fight but it ran out of puff," said a senior dealer at a Sydney-based brokerage.
Others echoed similar sentiments, saying investor interest had been been on both sides, rather than one-way traffic.

"There is a bit of activity out there but it is all two way business. There is not really much that is affecting prices," said Jamie Spiteri, dealer at Shaw Stockbroking, adding that much of the market's current action had more to do with bond yields than anything else.
"In the short term, the market is being dictated to by bond yields."
A well underpinned, but narrowly traded, bond market supported Spiteri's view of the day's proceedings.

News Corp's preferred ordinary shares topped turnover lists with nearly 43 million worth A$245 million traded. The bulk of it was in six lines totalling 40 million specialled through First Pacific Stockbroking.
Market speculation centred on U.S. investor Ron Perelman lightening the swag of News preferred ordinary ADRs he received when New acquired New World Communications last year.
News ordinary shares received a fillip with the perceived overhang gone, jumping over two percent to A$6.84.
Building material stocks lost some recent gains as last week's highs proved too tempting for profit-takers.
Pioneer International ended six cents lower at A$4.14, CSR lost 13.9 cents to A$4.811 while Boral lost three cents to A$3.85.
Results came from diamond miner Ashton Mining, which posted a year net profit of A$20.57 million. Its shares ended four cents lower at A$1.98 on light volume.
Grocery group Davids Ltd lost two cents to A$1.52 after it reported a 17.4 percent lower first half net profit of A$24.15 million.
Rises shaded falls just by a whisker, while about 30 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Futures trade was active, while options trade was much busier than recent days.
Total options traded 39,249 (17,738)
Turnover in March SPI contracts totalled 8,012 (6,739)

In other local markets, Australian bonds firmed after a good response to a T-bond tender and comments by Treasurer Costello that were seen as downplaying perceptions that the RBA had ruled out a rate cut. The market focus was now on Thursday's labour force report.

By 5.15 p.m. (0615 GMT), 10 year T-bonds were yielding 7.79 percent, down from Monday's 7.80 percent close.
The Australian dollar stumbled from early highs at the close Tuesday as a failure to clear 79 cent resistance prompted profit-taking.
Traders said the market was also been unsettled by reports Treasurer Peter Costello had said another cut in domestic interest rates could not be ruled out.
By 5.15 p.m. (0615 GMT), the local dollar was back at US$0.7880/90 having been rebuffed at 79 cents, but still up on the US$0.7860/65 seen late Monday.
